title: percentile is off by one and crashes at p=100
body: `percentile` in `metrics/percentiles.py` is documented to use the nearest-rank method: sort the values, then take rank `ceil(p / 100 * n)` (at least 1), counting from 1. It does not sort its input, it picks the wrong element whenever `p / 100 * n` is a whole number, and `p=100` raises `IndexError`. Please fix it. It must not modify the list it is given. An empty list, or a `p` outside 0 to 100, should raise `ValueError`.
